fact.text: Swiss filmmaker Daniel Schmid grew up inside a hotel, the Schweizerhof in Flims, and later returned to shoot many of his films there.

heads_up: Nalšios šiaurinėje apygardoje vyksta pirmalaikiai Seimo rinkimai, iš anksto balsavo 2,37 proc.
Ketvirtadienį Prancūzijoje streikai: atšaukiami regioniniai traukiniai, galimi skrydžių trikdžiai.

lithuania.headline: „Orlen“ svarsto atsisakyti Mažeikių gamyklos modernizacijos – gresia uždarymas
lithuania.summary: „Orlen“ vadovas Ireneuszas Fafara sako, kad grupė svarsto atsisakyti 600–700 mln. JAV dolerių kainuosiančio Mažeikių gamyklos atnaujinimo, o tada tektų svarstyti ir vienintelės Baltijos šalyse naftos perdirbimo gamyklos uždarymą. Pasak jo, gamyklos pelno nepakanka investicijai atsipirkti.
lithuania.context: „Orlen“ gamyklą valdo jau 20 metų ir į ją investavo daugiau kaip 5 mlrd. dolerių; 2025 m. lapkritį nutraukta sutartis su „Petrofac“ dėl strigusio modernizavimo projekto.

lithuania.headline: Seime svarstoma atidėti dalį paramos šeimoms priemonių
lithuania.summary: Seimo pirmininkas Juozas Olekas sako, kad dalį 2027 m. biudžete numatytų paramos šeimoms priemonių galima atidėti, o lėšas nukreipti kitur; biudžete numatytas 3,8 proc. BVP deficitas ir daugiau kaip 4,8 mlrd. eurų (5 proc. BVP) gynybai.
lithuania.context: Vyriausybė Seimui pateikė 2027 m. biudžetą su didesnėmis išlaidomis gynybai, pensijoms ir algoms. Prezidentas Nausėda ją kritikavo, kad nėra plano mažinti deficito, kuris kitąmet greičiausiai viršys ES leidžiamus 3 proc. BVP. Koalicijoje kilo ir ginčas tarp „valstiečių“ ir dalies socialdemokratų.

lithuania.headline: Iš Lietuvos išsiųsti trys ukrainiečiai, dirbę priešiškoms žvalgyboms
lithuania.summary: VSD pranešė, kad trys Ukrainos piliečiai už pinigus vykdė priešiškų žvalgybų užduotis, gautas per „Telegram“ ir kitas programėles; jų leidimai gyventi panaikinti, jie išsiųsti su penkerių metų draudimu grįžti.

world.headline: Vance blames Iran war for Republicans' midterm defeat
world.summary: In a 600-word post on X, Vice-President JD Vance wrote that "the reason we lost is the war" with Iran, an unusually sharp public break with the president. Trump agreed the midterms were "largely" decided by the war but said he would "do it again".
world.why: Covered by 6 outlets, top of BBC and Google News
world.context: The US and Israel attacked Iran in February, and the war pushed up petrol prices. In Tuesday's midterms Democrats won control of both the House and the Senate. Vance is seen as a likely 2028 presidential candidate.

world.headline: Joshua Wong jailed for 10 years in Hong Kong
world.summary: Joshua Wong, 30, was sentenced to 10 years for colluding with foreign forces after pleading guilty to working with exiled activist Nathan Law to seek sanctions on China. He had been due for release in January after nearly six years in jail.
world.context: Wong became the teenage face of Hong Kong's 2014 Umbrella protests. After huge pro-democracy protests in 2019, Beijing imposed a national security law in 2020, and hundreds were arrested under it. Wong was already serving a subversion sentence over an unofficial primary election.

world.headline: Israel's president opens coalition talks after Netanyahu loses majority
world.summary: President Isaac Herzog accepted the certified results and began consultations on who should form a government, after officials rejected Netanyahu's fraud claims. Netanyahu's bloc won 53 of 120 seats, Gadi Eisenkot's 48, and Arab-led parties a record 19.
world.context: Netanyahu has led Israel for most of the past 17 years. In the 27 October election he and his allies lost their majority, and his camp then accused Arab-led parties of "stealing" the vote.

world.headline: ANC narrowly leads in South Africa's local elections
world.summary: Early results show the ANC narrowly ahead of the Democratic Alliance in municipal elections, with a record 29.2 million registered; polls had put the ANC below a third of the vote amid anger over water and power cuts.
world.context: The ANC has governed since Nelson Mandela led it to power at the end of apartheid in 1994. Its support has fallen steadily, to 40.2% in the 2024 national election, when it lost its majority and had to form a coalition.

interesting.headline: LIV Golf to wind down after backer pulls out
interesting.summary: LIV Golf is expected to tell a court on Thursday that its planned revamp is not viable, after BC Partners decided against providing about $300m in financing. Saudi Arabia's PIF had pulled its backing in April, and LIV filed for bankruptcy protection in September.
interesting.context: LIV is the breakaway, Saudi-funded golf tour that launched in 2022 and split the sport.

interesting.headline: Spider-Man gives AMC its best quarter ever
interesting.summary: 'Spider-Man: Brand New Day' and 'The Odyssey' lifted AMC Theatres to record quarterly revenue of $1.71bn, up 31.6% on a year earlier; Spider-Man also boosted Sony Pictures' sales by 37%.

interesting.headline: Canva cuts 22% of its staff
interesting.summary: Canva is laying off 1,271 people as growth slows for the first time in a decade; it has cut its revenue growth forecast to 20% from 30% because of rising AI costs and faces competition from chatbots that make images.

interesting.headline: Hackers used iOS and Android flaws to infect phones
interesting.summary: Security firm Sekoia says hackers, likely from Russia's foreign intelligence service, used already-patched iOS and Android flaws on fake and hacked websites, including copies of an America 250 site and a London hotel near Downing Street, to steal cookies and device data.

ongoing.title: Russia-Ukraine war
ongoing.update: The confirmed death toll from Monday's Russian glide-bomb strike on an aid point and shelter in Komyshuvakha rose to 40, with more than 30 feared under the rubble. Zelensky spoke with US envoys Witkoff and Kushner ahead of three-way talks in Abu Dhabi on 10–11 November, and drones hit Russia's Ryazan refinery overnight.
ongoing.context: Russia launched its full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022, after seizing Crimea in 2014. Ukraine pushed Russian troops back from Kyiv, but the front has since become a long war of attrition, with heavy strikes on cities and energy. US-brokered peace talks have repeatedly stalled.

ongoing.title: US-Iran tensions
ongoing.update: Iran's Revolutionary Guards said two tankers and a tugboat caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz after using an 'unauthorised route', and South Korea said it will extend its naval unit's operations closer to the strait. Iranian leaders said the US midterm results showed voters rejected the war.
ongoing.context: Tensions grew after the US left the 2015 nuclear deal in 2018. In February the US and Israel attacked Iran, and Iran has since largely closed the Strait of Hormuz, a key route for world oil.

ongoing.title: Cyber-attacks on European refrigeration systems
ongoing.update: France's blood service EFS said hackers raised temperatures in cold rooms storing blood, though staff stepped in and no blood was lost; Poland also reported a hacked refrigeration system, while Lithuanian retailers say they were spared.
ongoing.context: In recent weeks hackers broke into remotely controlled supermarket refrigeration systems in at least 11 European countries. The EU called the attacks 'not isolated' and promised a joint response.

ongoing.title: Protests across France and Europe
ongoing.update: France faces another nationwide strike day on Thursday, with hundreds of thousands expected to march and rail, air traffic, hospital and teaching staff joining; thousands of Danish students also protested against cuts to student grants.
ongoing.context: Protests over living costs and education began in France and spread across Europe this autumn, after large unrest in October. Unions have called for coordinated Europe-wide rallies on 20 November.
